summary: ARPAWOCKY is a humorous poem, a parody of Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky, rewritten with ARPANET terms such as FTP, RJE, NCP, IMPs and RFNMs. It has no technical content.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 527 is a short poem built around ARPANET terminology. It uses names such as FTP, NCP, IMP, and RFNM in a playful verse.

subtitle: A poem that recasts ARPANET terms in a nonsense-verse style.

tldr.problem: The RFC presents no technical problem; it is a poem using network terminology.
tldr.mechanism: The verse places terms such as FTP, RJE, NCP, IMP, and RFNM in a playful rhyme and refrain.
tldr.outcome: It offers a humorous use of early ARPANET vocabulary rather than a protocol specification.

sections.title: ARPAWOCKY
sections.content: RFC 527, titled ARPAWOCKY, is a poem in verse. It repeats the line about protocols doing USER-SERVER and FTP and RJE, and uses technical vocabulary in rhyming stanzas.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC is a poem, not a technical manual. Its verse uses terms from network work.

sections.title: Network Terms in the Poem
sections.content: The poem mentions FTP, RJE, NCP, HOST-to-IMP, IMP-to-IMP, packets, ACK, NACK, and RFNM. These terms appear as part of the poem's imagery and rhyme rather than as formal definitions.
sections.plainLanguage: The verse includes names of protocols, computers, messages, and acknowledgements. It does not explain how those things work.

sections.title: A Non-Technical RFC
sections.content: The document is a literary piece, not a specification. Its content consists of the poem and its signature, with no protocol requirements or implementation instructions.
sections.plainLanguage: There are no technical instructions in this RFC. It uses network vocabulary for humor and rhyme.
